attributes.title: Level 1

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about using namespaces in your code to create new sprite kinds and access additional functions.

questions.hint: What words and symbols are used to declare a new sprite kind in JavaScript?
questions.title: [Select one] What is the correct way to declare a new sprite kind in the SpriteKind namespace?
questions.correctResponse: A new sprite kind is declared by typing the keyword let, the sprite kind name, an assignment operator, and the SpriteKind.create() function.

questions.hint: What keyword tells the program to use the sprite kind code outside of the namespace’s block statement?
questions.title: [Select one] The keyword ___________ needs to be used so that the sprite kind declared within the namespace’s block statement can be used in the rest of the project.
questions.correctResponse: Using the keyword export allows the sprite kind to be used in the project, outside of the namespace.

questions.hint: What keyword and symbol should be used to access the “secret menu”?
questions.title: [Select one] How can you access the “secret menu” functions, properties, and parameters?

answers.text: Type secretMenu, followed by a dot operator .
Type function, followed by a dot operator .
Type properties, followed by a dot operator .
Type the namespace, followed by a dot operator .

questions.correctResponse: Typing the namespace followed by a dot operator will open the code completion tool and reveal functions, properties, and parameters.

questions.hint: How do you create a new sprite kind in the JavaScript editor?
questions.title: [Select one] You can only create new sprite kinds in the blocks editor.
questions.correctResponse: In the JavaScript editor, you can create a new sprite kind using a namespace.

questions.title: [Open response] What are some new possibilities that you'll unlock in this level by learning about namespaces?
questions.correctResponse: A namespace can be used to create new sprite kinds and access other functions, properties, and parameters.

subgroups.title: Namespaces!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about using namespaces in your code to create new sprite kinds and access additional functions.

attributes.description: Welcome to Level 1 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about sprite kinds and sprite overlap events. In the JavaScript editor, you can use a namespace to create new sprite kinds. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 1:

badges.title: One of a Kind
badges.description: Use sprite kinds and events to control what happens to sprites in a project in JavaScript.

badges.title: A Meeting of the Kinds
badges.description: Use an overlap event that runs based on the sprites’ kinds.

badges.title: Nice Knowing Ya
badges.description: Write code that destroys a sprite.

badges.title: Life of the Party
badges.description: Set the value of the Player’s life.

badges.title: From One Sprite to Another
badges.description: Create a projectile that starts from the position of an existing sprite.

badges.title: Metamorphosis
badges.description: Change the sprite kind of an existing sprite.

badges.title: Kind of You to Join
badges.description: Create a new sprite kind in JavaScript.

badges.title: New Kind on the Block
badges.description: Write code that runs when a sprite with a specific sprite kind is created.

badges.title: Out of Chances
badges.description: Write code that runs when the Player’s life reaches zero.

badges.title: Spice Up Your Life
badges.description: Set the image used to represent the Player’s life.
